candidates.content_text:
Build your career with an organisation that is invested in your success. 
Maker Consulting Services is looking for a motivated Civil Engineering Undergraduate or Graduate to join our growing Newcastle team. Whether you're currently studying and looking to gain meaningful industry experience alongside university; or completing your degree and ready to begin your graduate career, this role offers the opportunity to develop your technical skills while contributing to real projects from day one. 
You'll work alongside experienced engineers on land development, infrastructure, roads and stormwater projects across Newcastle, the Hunter and broader NSW, gaining practical experience that complements your university studies and builds the foundation for your professional career. 
At Maker, we believe in providing a flexible work lifestyle. This has inspired us to change the way we work, leaving behind the traditional 5-day work week. Instead, Maker has adopted a 4-day work week, providing you with a day off during the week and giving you the time to catch up on life and do more of what you love!  
For undergraduate candidates, we offer flexibility around university timetables and exam periods, allowing you to gain consistent industry experience while completing your degree. 
Why join Maker 
Maker is a fast-growing, multi-disciplinary consultancy with more than 65 employees across 4 offices in NSW and Victoria. In addition to Civil Engineering, we specialise in Town Planning, Surveying, and Project Management which provides you with the opportunity to collaborate across a wide range of exciting projects. 
You’ll enjoy:
- Hands-on mentoring from experienced civil engineers, including direct exposure to senior members of our Newcastle team.  
- Real project involvement from the outset - not just observation or administrative tasks.  
- Experience across land development, roads, stormwater, infrastructure and multidisciplinary projects.  
- Opportunities to develop your skills in industry-standard civil design and modelling software.  
- A supportive culture where questions are encouraged and knowledge is shared. 
- The opportunity to grow from undergraduate engineer through to graduate and increasingly independent project responsibilities.  
- A 4-day working week, giving you more time to enjoy life outside work 
- Modern offices and regular team social events 
About the Role 
Located in our Newcastle office and working closely with our Newcastle Principal Civil Engineer, you will be exposed to a variety of projects that will introduce you to a broad range of civil engineering disciplines and progressively build your technical and professional capability. 
Your responsibilities will include: 
- Assisting with the design and documentation of civil infrastructure and land development projects, including roads, earthworks, stormwater drainage and utility infrastructure. 
- Developing practical experience using industry-standard civil design and modelling software. 
- Assisting with engineering calculations, technical assessments and preparation of reports. 
- Working with engineers, surveyors, planners and project managers to understand how projects progress from concept through to construction. 
- Participating in site inspections, project meetings and coordination activities where appropriate. 
You'll be encouraged to ask questions, learn from experienced professionals and progressively take on greater responsibility as your confidence grows. 
For undergraduate candidates, our aim is to provide meaningful, ongoing employment throughout your studies, with flexible part-time arrangements to suit university commitments and the opportunity to transition into a graduate position as you complete your degree. 
About You 
We're looking for someone curious, motivated and excited to build a career in Civil Engineering. 
We're looking for:
- Someone currently studying a Bachelor's degree in Civil or Environmental Engineering, or who has recently graduated from a relevant engineering degree. 
- A genuine interest in civil engineering and a willingness to learn. 
- An interest in design, problem-solving and seeing projects progress from concept through to construction. 
- Good written and verbal communication skills, with an interest in developing your technical writing capability. 
- Good time management, organisation and prioritisation skills. 
- The ability to work both independently and as part of a collaborative team. 
Whether you're part-way through your degree and looking to build industry experience alongside your studies, or approaching graduation and ready to begin your professional career, we'd like to hear from you. 
Ready to Build Your Career? 
If you're looking to gain meaningful civil engineering experience while completing your degree, or you're ready to take the first step in your graduate career, we'd love to hear from you. 
Please submit your resume and a short cover letter telling us a little about yourself, your studies and why you're interested in joining Maker by clicking the APPLY button.

Kickstart Your Career in Engineering Drafting! 
Ready to turn your interest in design and engineering into a career? 
Whether you’re finishing Year 12, recently left school or studying Drafting at TAFE, this is your opportunity to get started in the engineering industry. 
STP Consultants is looking for an enthusiastic Junior Structural Draftsperson to join our growing Brisbane team. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers and drafters, gain hands-on experience and learn how the drawings you create become part of real projects across Queensland. 
You don’t need years of experience. We’re looking for someone with the right attitude, curiosity and willingness to learn. 
Why you’ll love working here 
Start building your career   Get hands-on experience from day one and develop practical Structural drafting skills while learning from experienced engineers and drafters. 
Work on real projects   Go beyond the classroom and see how structural engineering projects come together. You’ll contribute to drawings and documentation used throughout projects from concept and design through to delivery. 
Learn from experienced people   Ask questions, share ideas and learn from people who genuinely want to help you develop. You’ll receive guidance and mentoring as your skills and confidence grow. 
Be part of a great team   Join a close-knit, collaborative team where people support each other, work together and enjoy what they do. 
Work in Fortitude Valley   Our Brisbane office is in the heart of Fortitude Valley, close to public transport, cafés, restaurants and everything the city has to offer.
The Opportunity  
As you develop your skills, you’ll have the opportunity to: 
- Assist with preparing structural drawings, plans and project documentation. 
- Work with engineers and experienced drafters to produce clear, accurate and high-quality drawings. 
- Learn industry standards, guidelines and best-practice drafting processes. 
- Develop your understanding of how structural engineering projects are designed and delivered. 
- Participate in project discussions and meetings to build your understanding of project requirements. 
- Carry out basic drawing and documentation checks with guidance from experienced team members. 
- Take on more responsibility as your skills and confidence develop. 
About you: 
You could be a great fit if you are: 
- A Year 12 student, recent school leaver, or currently studying Residential Drafting, or an equivalent qualification at TAFE.
- Genuinely interested in structural drafting, design and engineering. 
- Curious and keen to learn new skills. 
- Detail-oriented and take pride in producing accurate work. 
- A good communicator who is comfortable asking questions and taking feedback. 
- Reliable, organised and willing to have a go at new challenges. 
- Someone who enjoys working with others and being part of a team. 
- An Australian Citizen or Permanent Resident. 
Most importantly, bring your enthusiasm and willingness to learn. We’ll help you turn it into a career. 
What’s in it for you? 
- 
Career development: Build your skills through hands-on experience, mentoring and ongoing professional development. 
- 
Flexibility: Enjoy a 9-day fortnight, flexible working hours and the option to purchase additional leave. 
- 
Competitive remuneration: A package that reflects your experience and contribution. 
- 
Recognition and rewards: Employee referral rewards and recognition programs. 
- 
Great culture: Work with supportive people in a friendly, collaborative environment, with regular team and social events. 
- 
Wellbeing support: Access to a confidential Employee Assistance Program. 
- 
Long-term opportunity: Build your career with an established, Australian-owned engineering consultancy. 
About STP Consultants  
For more than 20 years, STP Consultants has been helping shape communities across Queensland. 
We’re a privately owned, multidisciplinary engineering consultancy, bringing together expertise across Civil, Structural, Mechanical, Electrical, Hydraulic, Fire and Seismic engineering. Our teams work on a diverse range of projects across Queensland, giving you the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals and see the many different paths an engineering career can take. 
Our values of Potential, Respect, Integrity, Deliver and Engage shape the way we work with our clients and with each other. 
We’re proud of our approachable leaders, supportive team environment and commitment to developing people and delivering quality engineering outcomes. 
Ready to get started?   
If you’re looking for more than just a first job and want to build a career in engineering, we’d love to hear from you. 
Click Apply and send us your Resume and Cover Letter. 
In your cover letter, tell us: 
1. Why you’re interested in starting a career in structural drafting.   
2. What interests you about joining STP Consultants. 
STP Consultants is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and welcome applications from all backgrounds.

Your Role 
As a Civil Engineer in the Army Reserve, you’ll get to use your existing qualifications in exciting new ways, applying your specialist skills to dynamic military environments. You’ll plan, design, coordinate, control and deliver a range of infrastructure engineering projects. 
This is a great opportunity to challenge yourself and work in exciting new environments, without compromising your current career goals.  
 Your duties may include: 
- aiding the community in humanitarian efforts 
- construction of field defences and obstacles 
- military and training duties 
- project managing the construction, repair and maintenance of roads, airfields, sea terminals, railways, buildings and bridges 
- providing terrain assessment advice 
- provision of construction materials and essential services such as water, electricity, and sewerage disposal 
- general soldiering duties, such as manning defensive positions, patrolling, traffic control, navigation, and camouflaging of vehicles and field equipment. 
Why join the Army Reserve?  
If you're looking for a new challenge, the Army Reserve could be for you. You'll enjoy the satisfaction of giving something back to Australia, while benefitting from:  
- Rewarding work that can be in complete contrast to your day job   
- Tax-free daily pay  
- Free healthcare and accommodation whilst on exercise or deployment  
- A flexible time commitment, ranging from a couple of weeks up to 150 days, with the potential to extend to 200 days  
- Easy to fit into your lifestyle with the option to work close to home   
- Comprehensive training   
- A supportive team environment  
- Can volunteer to deploy overseas 
- Friendships that last a lifetime  
- No minimum period of service, allowing you to leave and come back to the Army Reserve whenever you like 
Boost Your Income 
On completion of your initial military and employment training, you could earn at least $283/day tax-free. 
The pay you receive in the Army Reserve goes straight into your pocket with no deductions for tax, and it increases as you gain seniority and experience. Additional amounts are paid for time spent on exercises and deployments. 
Eligibility:
For this role, you must:  
- Be at least 17 at the time of enlistment and an Australian Citizen.  
- If you are not an Australian Citizen you may still be eligible to join the ADF if you meet certain criteria, please visit the ADF Careers Eligibility Page for more details  
- Be reasonably fit and healthy. Keeping fit is a big part of joining the ADF. You’ll need to pass a physical fitness test before you join, but don’t worry, we'll give you tips to help you prepare.  
- Be able to successfully obtain a security clearance. 
- Hold a Bachelor of Civil Engineering or a related discipline 
- Have had training in a branch of engineering with the practical experience required for graduate membership of the Institution of Engineers Australia (IEAust), or another chartered institution of similar status. 
Apply Now  
Apply today or request more information by calling 13 19 01 or emailing  applications@adfcareers.gov.au.

- Coordinating with clients, councils, service authorities, contractors and project teams.  
- Managing deliverables from planning and approvals through to construction.  
- Developing practical and innovative engineering solutions.  
- Providing guidance and mentoring to graduate and junior engineers. 
About You

Most importantly, you're looking for a place where you can continue developing as an engineer, project leader and mentor.

Ready for What's Next?

 Our client is delivering the major civil works package on a large-scale renewable energy project in rural Queensland, and they're looking for an experienced Project Engineer – Civil to join the project team and play a key role in delivering complex civil construction works.
 Reporting to the Project Manager / Senior Project Engineer, you'll be responsible for managing and coordinating civil construction activities, making sure the work is delivered safely, efficiently and in line with contractual requirements.

- Accommodation and meals supplied.

- Collaborative and supportive project team.

Cadet Estimator & Project Coordinator — Commercial Waterproofing
Loganholme, Brisbane QLD | Full-Time | $65,000–$75,000 + Super + Vehicle Allowance
The role
Concreteseal is a specialist waterproofing company based in Loganholme, working on commercial construction projects across South East Queensland — multi-level developments, mixed-use buildings, podium decks, planter boxes, basements and remedial work.
We are seeking a Cadet Estimator & Project Coordinator to support our commercial estimating function. The role is structured as a cadetship: you will begin on measured take-offs and bills of quantities under direct supervision, and progress toward preparing and defending complete tender submissions. It also carries genuine involvement in project documentation, procurement and site coordination, so you understand how the work you price is delivered.
Prior waterproofing experience is not required. Numerical ability, attention to detail and a willingness to learn the technical side are.
Studying? That's exactly who we want
If you're part-way through any of the following — apply. You do not need to have finished it.
- A university degree in construction management, quantity surveying, civil or structural engineering, architecture, property or building surveying — including a first- or second-year student looking for industry experience alongside study, or someone who has paused a degree and wants to return to it while working.
- A Certificate IV, Diploma or Advanced Diploma in Building and Construction.
- A trade qualification in waterproofing or a related trade.
- Any related qualification you're about to start, or have finished and now need the site and commercial experience to go with.
We'll work around lecture, class and assessment commitments, put you on the kind of live projects your coursework keeps referring to, and support you toward the licensing and industry training that follows.
Half-finished study isn't a gap on your resume here. It's the reason we're interested.
What the job actually is
This is a commercial-weighted role. The bulk of your week sits in estimating and tender work, with real involvement in documentation, procurement and project delivery.
Estimating & tendering (the core of the role)
- Review architectural and structural drawings, specifications and waterproofing consultant reports.
- Complete measured take-offs from plans — areas, perimeters, penetrations, upturns, junctions.
- Build and maintain bills of quantities for tender submissions.
- Price labour, materials, plant, access and preliminaries against real rates, not guesses.
- Prepare tender submissions, qualifications, exclusions and alternative system proposals.
- Track tender opportunities, submission deadlines, RFIs and addenda.
- Follow up submitted tenders and chase outcomes.
- Review incoming subcontract agreements for scope gaps, onerous clauses and pricing risk before they're signed.
- Sit in on pricing reviews with management and learn how a commercial rate is actually built.
Project documentation & QA
Commercial builders don't just want a price — they want the paperwork.
- Produce and maintain ITPs, QMPs, SWMS and project quality documentation.
- Compile product data sheets, warranties, technical submissions and compliance documentation for builder approval.
- Maintain project records — hold point sign-offs, inspection records, flood test documentation, site photography.
- Prepare and price variations, and get them approved before the work is done.
- Keep documentation aligned to AS 3740, AS 4654.1/.2 and the NCC.
Project & site coordination
- Issue scopes of work, job packs and work orders to site crews.
- Coordinate crew allocation, site access, inductions, deliveries and program dates with builders and other trades.
- Chase the information that holds jobs up — drawings, approvals, preceding trades, screed and tiling sequencing.
- Attend site when required for measure-ups, pre-start walk-throughs and progress checks.
- Keep builders informed before they have to ask.
Procurement & materials
- Raise purchase orders and obtain supplier pricing and lead times.
- Confirm product availability and delivery dates against the program.
- Make sure the right systems and materials are on site before the crew is.
- Resolve short deliveries, incorrect product and supply issues.
- Build working relationships with our suppliers and technical reps.
Who we're after
You don't need to know waterproofing. You need to be organised, numerate, and hard to rattle.
Essential:
- Strong numerical and spreadsheet ability.
- Good written English — you'll be corresponding with project managers and contract administrators daily.
- Attention to detail. A missed 200 square metres on a take-off is a real problem.
- The ability to run several tenders and several live jobs at once without dropping either.
- Willingness to say "I don't know" and then go and find out.
- Current Australian driver's licence.
Well regarded:
- A construction-related qualification — trade certificate, diploma or university degree — completed, in progress, or about to start.
- Any construction, trade services, remedial, roofing, concreting, flooring or building background.
- Experience reading construction drawings and specifications.
- Take-off or estimating software (Bluebeam, Cubit, Buildsoft or similar).
- Exposure to tier-2 or tier-3 builder documentation requirements.
If you've come off the tools and want a commercial career, or you're studying building and construction and want the estimating side of it rather than another labouring job, this is a good fit.
What you get
- $65,000–$75,000 + super + vehicle allowance, reviewed on performance rather than on a calendar.
- Direct training from the Operations Manager — no layers between you and the person doing the pricing.
- Exposure to live commercial tenders from day one, not after a probation period.
- Flexibility around study commitments, and support toward relevant qualifications and industry training.
- A small team where your work is visible and your judgement gets used.
- Genuine progression: Cadet Estimator → Estimator → Senior Estimator or Project Manager. We're growing and we'd rather promote than recruit.
About Concreteseal
Concreteseal is a Queensland family-owned waterproofing company based in Loganholme, servicing Brisbane, Logan, the Gold Coast and the wider South East Queensland corridor.
We work for commercial builders on multi-level developments, mixed-use buildings, aged care, education, industrial and remedial projects. Our work covers liquid membranes, sheet membranes, polyurea and polyurethane systems, injection and remedial waterproofing, and below-ground tanking.
We hold our own trade qualifications and we do our own work — we don't broker it out. That's why the documentation and the pricing have to be right.
To apply
Click Apply and attach your resume, along with a short covering note explaining why estimating interests you. If you're studying, tell us what you're doing and where you're up to. You don't need to address every point above.
Applications are reviewed as they're received, so we'd encourage you to apply early. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.
You must have the right to work in Australia. No agencies, please.
